links.outcome: Agreement and diagnostic accuracy of ChatGPT 4.0 versus epileptologists for epilepsy diagnosis
links.effect: Cohen's kappa -0.01 (95% CI -0.08 to 0.06); sensitivity 17.6%, specificity 81.4%; errors in 41.7% of cases; epilepsy diagnosed in 18.2% by ChatGPT vs 36.2% by neurologists.
links.quote: ChatGPT 4.0 does not reach human clinicians' performance in diagnosing epilepsy, showing poor performance in identifying epilepsy but better at recognizing non-epileptic cases.

links.outcome: Factors associated with ChatGPT diagnostic errors, including patient age and medical conditions
links.effect: ChatGPT made diagnostic errors in 41.7% of cases, more frequent in older patients and those with specific medical conditions; correct classification associated with acute symptomatic seizures of unknown etiology.
links.quote: ChatGPT made diagnostic errors in 41.7% of the cases, with errors more frequent in older patients and those with specific medical conditions.

screen.reason: Retrospective study evaluating the diagnostic accuracy of ChatGPT-4 for epilepsy against clinical expert diagnoses, without testing an organizational deployment practice or safeguard.
